page_title: Building an image caption generator with Deep Learning in Tensorflow

summary.title: Building an image caption generator with Deep Learning in Tensorflow
summary.one_liner: You learn how a CNN encoder and LSTM decoder combine into a Show and Tell style image captioner, use beam search for better captions, and run a pre-trained Tensorflow model in Docker to caption your own images.
keywords: how to caption images with deep learning
takeaways: A CNN produces an image embedding that is used as the initial state of an LSTM language model.
Caption generation can be framed as a graph search; greedy sampling is cheap but can be suboptimal.
Beam search keeps the top N candidate sentences at each step, trading some compute for better captions.
The tutorial walks through a Dockerized Tensorflow setup, downloading a pre-trained Show and Tell model trained on MSCOCO, and running inference on your own images.
summary.summary: Cole Murray explains the Show and Tell architecture from Google's 2014 paper, where a CNN encodes an image into a dense embedding that seeds an LSTM which generates a caption word by word. The article covers captions as a search problem and why beam search is a practical middle ground between greedy decoding and exhaustive search. It then provides a hands-on section: building a Docker image with Tensorflow, downloading the pre-trained model and vocabulary file, and running an inference script that prints candidate captions with log probabilities. Prerequisites are basic knowledge of CNNs, LSTMs, and Tensorflow.
